items.title: SO-Arena: Benchmarking the Capability Spectrum and Reliability of System One Models
items.summary: System One models promise fast, general-purpose decision-making without lengthy token generation. However, understanding their capability spectrum and decision reliability requires more than aggregate performance on current benchmarks. Existing evaluations often provide limited insight into the breadth of model capabilities and the reliability of their decisions. items.title: BirdDreams: Joint Perspective and BEV Video Generation for a Plausible, Reactive Driving World Model
items.summary: Driving world models aim to simulate how a scene unfolds under different ego actions. This requires plausible motion of surrounding vehicles as well as precise ego-trajectory control. Learning vehicle motion from perspective video alone is challenging because motion is entangled with appearance and vehicles can be occluded. items.title: Scaling Mathematical Proof Supervision from Structured Textbooks
items.summary: Mathematical supervision for language models is typically flattened into isolated problem-solution pairs, discarding the curricular organization and evidential structure of the original sources. items.title: PhysLoop: Harnessing LLMs' Physics Awareness for Self-Improving Video Generation Models
items.summary: Video generation models produce visually realistic videos but still struggle with physical dynamics and causal consistency. Learning from generated videos requires fine-grained physical supervision, yet reliable quality judgments, correction pairs, and controlled variations are difficult to obtain. items.title: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation
items.summary: Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation. items.title: Duo: A Reciprocal World Model for Full-Duplex Interaction
items.summary: In this report, we introduce the Reciprocal World Model (RWM) and present Duo v1, a full-duplex world model that continuously perceives audiovisual inputs while responding to users in real time. items.title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
items.summary: Low-bit quantization reduces the inference cost of LLM agents but can compromise task success. items.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary: Decision models answer a question with a typed output, such as a choice among options with a probability for each, so one model can choose an agent's actions, evaluate actions already taken, or score every action to teach a policy with reinforcement learning. items.title: Open Vision Banana: A Fully Open Recipe for Generative Visual Perception
items.summary: Recent work suggests that pretrained image generators encode real-world understanding beyond image synthesis. Vision Banana exploits this by framing vision tasks as conditional image editing. However, its data, weights, code, and implementation details are not public. items.title: On the Design of Hyper-Connections: Simplification, Stability, and Scalability
items.summary: Hyper-Connections (HC) architectures are increasingly adopted in frontier language models, yet their components remain insufficiently understood and introduce non-negligible training overhead. items.summary: Large foundation models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 have recently been shown to control robots directly from visual observations. items.title: Read Less, Solve More: Token-Efficient Sparse Reading of External Content for AI Agents
items.summary: Web-facing AI agents repeatedly access webpages, documents, repositories, and tool responses, yet reading interfaces often expose entire objects when only sparse evidence is needed. items.summary: Decoder-only Large View Synthesis Models (LVSMs) with KV-cache have recently achieved state-of-the-art quality by regressing novel views from neural networks without reconstructing 3D geometry, while Test-Time Training (TTT) layers save computation but sacrifice quality. items.summary: Multimodal coding agents decouple 4D world construction from visual generation, repurposing video models from world generators toward generative renderers. items.title: Interactive Visual Gym: Evaluating Visual Interaction Models with Simulated Users in Interactive Worlds
items.summary: Visual interaction models that support users during ongoing physical tasks require evaluation in closed loop, where assistant responses can change subsequent user behavior and task outcomes. items.title: UniSpark: Exploring Hybrid Attention for Multimodal Understanding and Generation
items.summary: We present UniSpark-9B, a unified multimodal model that investigates hybrid attention for visual understanding and generation. Built on a Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts backbone with approximately 9B parameters in each branch, UniSpark combines full attention for explicit token interactions with GatedDeltaNet linear attention for compact context propagation. items.title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
items.summary: Agentic workloads are a major source of LLM inference demand. Existing prefill--decode (PD) disaggregated serving systems offer limited flexibility for runtime adaptation of compute allocation and KV cache management, and rely on coarse signals that only partly capture the diverse and dynamic agent workload. items.summary: How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. Most models use a pretrained vision encoder, while some recent recipes train the encoder from scratch with the language model or remove it entirely. items.summary: Self-improving embodied agents are increasingly being developed and compared on robot simulation benchmarks. items.summary: We present FAME-QP, a GPU-accelerated solver for dense quadratic programs arising in linear model predictive control. items.summary: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that neural networks are converging toward similar representation spaces. items.title: Subliminal Learning in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Subliminal learning is a phenomenon in large language models (LLMs) where a teacher passes a hidden preference to a student through training data unrelated to that preference. items.title: DeepStress: Stress-Testing Deep Search Agents
items.summary: While search agents demonstrate impressive capabilities in multi-step question answering, their robustness to poor-quality evidence remains under-explored. We study a different allocation: store 8-bit weights, decode with their top 4 bits, and redo a step at 8 bits only when the low-precision output distribution looks uncertain (entropy above a threshold or a small top-two margin).
